routes.label: Compare points from the two groups of attempts

question: In a recent basketball game, Shenille attempted only three-point shots and two-point shots. She was successful on \(20\%\) of her three-point shots and \(30\%\) of her two-point shots. Shenille attempted \(30\) shots. How many points did she score?
solution:
The useful observation is that the point value times the success rate is the same for both types of shot:
\[
3\cdot0.20=0.6,
\qquad
2\cdot0.30=0.6.
\]
Let \(u\) and \(v\) be the numbers of three-point and two-point attempts, respectively. Every attempt belongs to exactly one group, so \(u+v=30\). She made \(0.20u\) three-point shots and \(0.30v\) two-point shots. Her total score was therefore
\[
3(0.20u)+2(0.30v)
=0.6(u+v)
=0.6\cdot30
=18.
\]
She scored \(18\) points, choice B.
